extracted.intended_audience: EPA staff, state regulators, researchers, and public stakeholders interested in biosolids policy and human health risk assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and agency response process examining the technical methods used to set chemical and pathogen standards for land-applied biosolids, with emphasis on protecting human health rather than ecological or agricultural effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of technical methods used to establish chemical standards for biosolids
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC was asked to conduct an independent evaluation of the technical methods and approaches used to establish the chemical standards for biosolids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should focus on whether the methods for setting chemical contaminant limits are scientifically sound and protective of human health; see linked NRC report and EPA technical background document for methods and data used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of technical methods used to establish pathogen standards for biosolids
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC was asked to conduct an independent evaluation of the technical methods and approaches used to establish the pathogen standards for biosolids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should examine the approaches to pathogen risk assessment, measurement, and control in land-applied biosolids; see 'Problem Formulation for Human Health Risk Assessments of Pathogens in Land-Applied Biosolids' and related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on human health protection (exclusion of ecological/agricultural issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC evaluation was to focus specifically on human health protection and not ecological or agricultural issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews, recommendations, and any changes should be evaluated primarily by their implications for human health risk; ecological or agricultural consequences were explicitly out of scope for this evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of existing sewage sludge regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted a review of existing sewage sludge (biosolids) regulations as part of its response to the NRC report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review assesses whether current regulatory requirements adequately protect human health and how regulations align with NRC findings; see EPA's Final Agency Response and fact sheet for outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of recommendations via EPA's 14-Point Action Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA released a 14-Point Action Plan in response to the 2002 NRC review to address identified issues and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of progress should track the 14 action items, their implementation status, and whether they remedy NRC-identified deficiencies; see 'Biosolids Update 14 Action Plan Projects' for project-level details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of exposure and hazard screening assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a Sewage Sludge Exposure and Hazard Screening Assessment to identify chemicals or pathways of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening assessments should use available exposure and hazard data to prioritize chemicals and support decisions about further assessment or regulatory action; see EPA's Technical Background Document for methods and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and monitoring methods for biosolids exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of exposure measurement approaches, as reflected in the Proceedings of the Biosolids Exposure Measurement Workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should include the adequacy of exposure measurement methods, data quality, and applicability to real-world land application scenarios when assessing risk and setting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem formulation for human health risk assessments of pathogens
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a clear problem formulation step when conducting human health risk assessments for pathogens in land-applied biosolids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem formulation should define assessment goals, exposure scenarios, susceptible populations, pathogen metrics, and decision context to ensure assessments are targeted and interpretable.
